reviews.comment: Honestly the lectures for this class were not explained super well. However if you read the textbook and struggle through the homeworks NOT all the night before they are due, you are 70% there imo. 206's a hard course for people who don't put the effort in but if you do the hw without ai you are bound to get the hang of it. He curved an A to 89.5%.

Great guy, bad teaching format. Most ppl don't learn by reading and going over basic slideshows. If students are struggling this much in a course, there's something wrong with how they're teaching it. Honestly, take don't panic with a professor that works through examples, not click through a slide like here's x; do this: page of calculations.

Mr. Youngs is an awesome professor. His lectures are insightful, however he does use Iclicker to track attendance. I often went to his office hours, which definitely helped me prepare for future exams and to understand the overall concepts better. He also gives extra credit and it is easy to raise your grade!

Professor Youngs did a decent job. He's a funny guy who tries his best not to make you panic. I will also say, no matter which professor you take for PHYS 206 & 207, there is an expectation for you to learn outside of class. That is just the norm.

Don't even bother with university physics, just take dont panic. Most of the class is self study and they will make sure to throw curveballs on every exam after the first which makes it hard to maintain an A

Physics definitely isn't an easy class, and I recognize that, but his lectures definitely didn't make it any easier. Lots of the learning is done in homework, lecture is nearly pointless and only worth showing up for iClicker. Bragged about having the highest percentages of A's in all 206 sections, also the highest percentage of D's.

PHYS 206 is just a hard class, and that's kinda an unavoidable fact. However, he does make a lot of the content seem a lot more advanced than it actually is, introduces a lot of confusion for exams. Would brag about having the highest percentage of A's in all the 206 sections but also the highest percentage of D's, so take that how you will!

Such a fun guy to listen to, homework was graded easily, as well as the group project. My one complaint is that the second exam was much harder than the first one, so pay attention to his lecture and take real notes.

this class is the most failed and most q-dropped class at tamu. make sure you read the textbook beforehand, pay attention in recitation and ask any questions during office hours. youngs is funny and cares about physics, however he is not the best at explaining problems step-by-step. i didn't find the lectures helpful. this is also my first c.

Dr Youngs made this course ten times easier than it would have been with any other professor. He was very easy to approach and would always help you to understand whatever topic you need. The homework load may be intimidating, but if you follow what he tells you, and do it before the due date, they are very helpful. 10/10 professor and very funny.

He's fine, really passionate about physics, if you take his class seriously, you'll for sure get at least a B. It was his first time teaching Physics for Presidents, so of course he wasn't perfect, but his lectures are really enjoyable.

He was very kind and I really enjoyed his class, although at one point he gave us an exam (completely different from exam 1) that was extremely difficult. The average was extremely low as well. Felt very unfair. But besides that once incident it was an extremely fun class and I enjoyed his lectures!

Dr Youngs taught PHYS 123 at A&M for one semester, and I happened to get him as my professor. He is funny, incredibly smart, and passionate about Physics. I'm not sure if he will teach it again, but he was a great teacher I absolutely recommend him! He wants you to succeed. Always email if you have questions or need help, great teacher!

He might be better in 207 but taking 206 was way harder than necessary. No one I've talked to has found his lectures helpful, and we all feel unprepared for the homework, and then even less prepared for the exams. Definitely take a professor with the don't panic textbook, as you learn physics better and have WAY less homework with them.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a very funny prof and he really cares about people's grades. You NEED to read the textbook ahead of time for a class like this or you will likely struggle. His lectures are great and he does have random in class Iclicker quizzes on some days that are overall worth 6% of your grade. DO NOT become complacent after the first exam!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: PHYS-206 is somewhat the same no matter your professor - every class is standardized. You will learn almost all material through reading the textbook, and class does not add much to that. Dr. Youngs is great at answering questions, but lectures were a little boring. His office hours were INCREDIBLE and where I learned most. Exams are all common.

PHYS 206 is designed to be a challenging course regardless of what professor you take to make ETAM more competitive. However, Dr. Youngs knows his stuff and answers questions pretty well. I just wished he taught the way the answered questions (aka use the whiteboard to walk through the questions).
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were very informative so I would highly recommend you attend them (+ IClicker). The textbook is also helpful for a more intuitive understanding but lecture + homework mostly suffices for the problem solving you would see in this class. If you just do the homework honestly and pay attention you should not have a hard time in this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Youngs explains concepts very clearly. He takes care to present things, particularly new concepts, in a way that students will be able to understand. He explains things on a deep level and gladly answers questions. He makes it clear what is expected of students and the classwork is not too intensive.

Before looking at any PHYS207 professor, just know this class is ridiculously difficult. That said, Dr. Youngs was a great professor. His lectures were clear and he explained topics as well as anyone could for this class, and he also had fun with us.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a great professor. He makes the lectures engaging. its easy to understand what he is saying. Your grade is influenced by attendance to lectures and the recitation. Quizzes have unlimited attempts. homeworks are long but are not necessary in preparing for the tests and can be cheated with chat gpt. This class is crammable with lecture notes.

Young's boasts about how difficult his material is and how many people fail or drop his class which doesn't make him very approachable. Most of the learning you'll do is from doing a ton of homework only to be hit with new questions on the exam. I can't recommend him as a prof. Try to find a different uni prof for 206 or DP for 207.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Although the material itself is difficult, Youngs certainly made it easier for me to understand. Lectures were helpful and posted on Canvas. Occasional iClickers. Did helpful reviews of material before exams. Highly recommend.

Dr. Youngs is a super good option if you decide to take 207 at A&M. He's one of the course coordinators, so he always knows what's going on in terms of the course content and schedule. He's always available through email and has office hours four days a week. You'll be fine if you go to class and recitation, do the homework, and study for exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: -Youngs' lectures were very scattered and he didn't teach us the concepts behind what we were learning.  He would hardly ever work out problems on the whiteboard, and just showed us pre-worked problems on a slideshow instead, with no notes or steps included on the screen.  This class is hard, and Youngs made it even harder.

This class is so free if you actually lock in and study properly, i had a 73 exam grade going into the third exam and finished with an 98 because of how the learning objectives stack in 206, youngs can be a bit corny but he really does care and is very willing to help.

(PHYS 201) This class is very difficult and I was lost the whole time, but Youngs is a good teacher and wants to see you succeed. I only took him because Jucos required a pre req and I was very nervous, but Youngs makes this class doable. Gave a curve on every test and partial credit as well. If you don't mind the possible hit to your GPA, take it.

He would get mad because people wouldn't show up to lecture and even yelled at someone for leaving early. Overall, pretty good lecturer but cares way too much about student attendance. I think if you took AP Physics, there's no point in going to class and instead use the time to do homework. He uses iClicker and for an 8AM, that got me a B.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty cool guy, pretty hard class. No professor is going to make this class easy if taken at A&M. Lot of fast paced content, really make sure you don't get behind with homework. If you can, probably take this class at a community college. If you have to take it at A&M Youngs is a good option.

(Took for PHYS207). PHYS207 was the hardest class I've had the displeasure of taking, but Mike made it not as bad. I'd recommend taking him in the afternoon since he thrives on class participation. If you do decide to take PHYS207 at TAMU, I wouldn't say Mike is my first choice for PHYS207 profs, but he isn't so bad if the other sections fill up.

(Took him for PHYS 207) Dr. Youngs is an amazing professor who truly cares about student learning. For myself, his lectures did not help me much since he only talked about the big concepts, and did not go into specific examples we would see on homeworks/exams. To truly understand the material, you WILL have to read the textbook outside of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Loved having him for 206 & 207. Lectures are clear and slides given. Content's inherently difficult, actually showing up to lecture, doing the HW, reviewing past exams, and putting in effort are enough to succeed. Also obviously helps to have some previous knowledge. I took Youngs when he had no reviews and I do not regret taking a chance w/ him.
Great professor. Explains concepts very elaborately and concisely. Fun guy as well.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Youngs was a great professor, he knew his stuff and was ready to help in office hours or after class with any questions I had. The lectures provide a good base understanding but the textbook helps a lot as well. His help made the course a lot easier for me as time went on.

Professor Young was super caring and attentive. He was always making jokes in class and didn't go to fast with his lectures. The textbook is really your best friend, and the lectures are extra help to better understand the concepts. If you read the textbook and do a bunch of practice problems, the tests shouldn't be too bad. Would take Youngs again
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Expected amount of homework, makes jokes during lectures and feels young and nerdy. I think this was his first year here from blinn. I finished with a 96 by only using practice exams to study, but I have taken physics before. Office hours were a bit of an issue for me and he was slow on emails, but if you can go he helps you a lot.

Youngs is a fantastic guy and cares about his students. His class is difficult (it's physics). Get your homework done at a reasonable time and make time for studying, and you will definitely make a better grade than me. Overall Youngs is the best professor you could possibly have for physics.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The guy is funny, and he definitely makes his lectures interesting. The problem is that he explains concepts way to quickly, which means that you don't really retain anything from class. Super nice guy though.

The course was difficult, but he's honestly the best professor I've had at A&M by far. He's great at explaining concepts, answers questions thoroughly during class, and reviews what we've done before exams. Never thought I'd look forward to an 8am lecture before his course.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class
